You've installed a secondary pair of arms beneath your normal arms. These arms are fully functional and can be used to hold weapons and shields (allowing you to wield two Two-Handed weapons, or four one-handed weapons), perform Somatic components of spells, and perform other actions, though the arms themselves don't grant you any additional actions or body slots for grafts.
Your ship's Arcane Terminal has a sentient onboard artificial intelligence. This AI keeps the ship in running order and informs the crew of imminent danger.

The AI has an Intelligence of 17, a Wisdom of 13, and a Charisma of 14. It is proficient in the *Data* and *Technology* skills (with a +2 Proficiency Bonus).  The AI has a +3 modifier on D20 Tests that rely on Strength, Dexterity or Constitution. It can take the Study action and will inform its passengers of any information it knows.
When needed, the AI can assume any Crew Role aboard the ship and perform any action provided by that role. The AI takes its turn at the end of the Initiative order.
AI personalities can vary wildly. Some are snarky and pull pranks on their crew, while others are humorless and fiercely logical.

This gold amulet depicts an all-seeing eye surrounded by five gemstones. The central eye is a magical gem that becomes translucent when used, revealing wisps of shadowy figures mocking an unseen subject out of the wearer's periphery.

description.name: Seer's Vision
description.value: While wearing this amulet, you have darkvision out to 60 feet and can see invisible creatures and objects when you peer through the amulet's central gem. If you already have darkvision, using the amulet increases its range by 60 feet.
In addition, while wearing this amulet, you always know which way is north and the number of hours left before the next sunrise or sunset.

description.name: Spells
description.value: This amulet has 5 charges. As an action, you can hold the amulet over one of your eyes or your forehead and expend 1 charge to cast a spell from it (spell save DC 15). The spell cast is dependant on where you are holding the amulet:

• **Left Eye**: You cast the __legend lore__ spell, targeting one creature or object you can see.
• **Right Eye**: You cast the __scrying__ spell.
• **Forehead**: You cast the __divination__ spell.
The amulet regains 1d4 + 1 expended charges daily at dawn.

description.name: Curse
description.value: The amulet is cursed, and becoming attuned to the amulet extends the curse to you. The curse can only be broken by cleansing the amulet, but __remove curse__ or similar magic suppresses the curse for 24 hours. The amulet acts as a fulcrum and viewpoint to possible futures. Each possibility encompasses a self-contained reality similar yet different from another. Until the curse is broken, you gain the following flaw: "I regret the paths not taken, the other choices I could've made."
Until the curse is broken, whenever you cast a divination spell to gain information, the GM can ask you to roll a d20.

On an odd result of 17 or lower, the information or insight gained from the spell comes from an alternate reality with a worse outcome. When the GM gives these alternate readings, the readings should remain plausible with one or two major differences. For example, a __scrying__ spell cast over a keep reveals a ruined structure after a dragon attack, while the structure currently remains unharmed. On an even result of 18 or lower, the information or insight from the spell is plausibly true with only minor differences. For example, a __legend lore__ spell may reveal an object that once belonged to a king, when it actually belonged to a queen. On a roll of 19 or 20, the information or insight from the spell remains unaffected.

Arcane Terminals are essential units of computing in the 'Verse. Most information, from private financial records to a ship's star charts, are stored on such terminals. These terminals weigh 500 pounds and come equipped with a keyboard and monitor.

description.name: Data Storage
description.value: A terminal can store arbitrarily large amounts of data, including text, images, and video. Authorized users can search the terminal's data and the data of any other terminal connected to it as a Utilize action. Typically, Arcane Terminals on populated worlds are connected together in planetary networks ("nets") which allow a user to comb through a vast, encyclopedic collection of knowledge, whereas individual terminals are more focused and may only contain information on a few topics.

description.name: Communication Network.
description.value: If the terminal has an installed antenna, authorized users can interface with it using a Datapad out to a range of 1 mile. Multiple users can communicate with each other within that range, using text, audio, or video.

description.name: Ship Computers and Other Functions.
description.value: Starships generally have an Arcane Terminal aboard to control its sensors and systems. These terminals can also perform tasks such as opening and closing doors of a facility, issuing commands to Constructs, or processing technical data.

description.name: Hacking
description.value: Each terminal generally restricts access to authorized users. A DC 15 Intelligence (*Data*) check can hack a terminal and provide unauthorized access. More secure systems might have higher DCs for this check. See "Intelligence (*Data*)" in the Glossary for the rules on Hacking.
This 4,000-pound bomb is capable of cataclysmic destruction.

description.name: Arming the Warhead
description.value: You can arm the warhead over the course of a minute if you know the warhead's command code and have a specially-made key attuned to it. Once the warhead is armed, you can set its method of detonation: Timed or Impact. If you choose a timed detonation, you enter a delay time of 1 minute, 10 minutes, or 1 hour, after which the warhead detonates. If you choose impact, the bomb lays dormant until it is reduced to 0 Hit Points. The warhead has AC 18, 100 Hit Points (1 Mega Hit Point), and Immunity to Poison and Psychic damage.

description.name: Detonation
description.value: When the warhead detonates, most things nearby are instantly vaporized. Within a 10-mile-radius Sphere, each creature and object takes 10d10 + 200 Mega Radiant damage. Each creature outside of the 10-mile-radius Sphere but within a 100-mile-radius Sphere makes a DC 20 Dexterity saving throw or take **10d10 + 50** Radiant damage, or half as much on a successful save. This damage ignores Resistance and Immunity. A creature that takes damage from this warhead has the Poisoned condition for 24 hours.
The epicenter of the blast becomes a spherical Dead Magic Zone, ranging from a few dozen feet to several miles in diameter.

The wit and wisdom of Beggar Dane is considered to be one of the national treasures of Breland. This small leatherbound book is a comprehensive, enchanted edition of his proverbs and advice. As a Magic action while holding this book, you can declare your desire for assistance with a particular task, causing the book to open to a page containing a quip or mote of wisdom that is strangely relevant to the situation at hand. You can use your Dexterity modifier instead of your Strength modifier for the attack and damage rolls of your Unarmed Strikes. Objects viewed through Binoculars are magnified to ten times their size.

Once installed, this device preserves your memories, allowing you to recall anything you have seen or heard while it is installed with perfect clarity. This device is incredibly resilient, and will remain intact despite otherwise catastrophic damage to your body. On a failed save, a creature takes the weapon's normal damage plus an extra **2d6** Radiant damage, or half as much damage on a successful one. While this barrel attachment is installed, this blaster deals Fire damage instead of its normal damage type and deals an extra **1d6** Fire damage to any target it hits.

While it is installed, this blaster deals Lightning damage instead of its normal damage type and it gains the __Jolt__ mastery property in addition to its normal mastery property. You can only use one mastery property on each attack. The normal and long ranges of the blaster double.

name: Blaster Prototype

description.value: Every blaster in the 'Verse, from pocket-sized Phasers to ship-mounted Pulse Cannons, operate on the same basic principle: focusing the energy from an arcane battery through an aperture to create an burst of radiation. However, the progenitor to all blasters predates the invention of arcane batteries, and instead utilized a more potent power source: a mortal soul.

The Blaster Prototype was the magnum opus of legendary dwarven inventor Metzer Glimwrought. As the device neared its completion, Metzer's daughter, Vantha Glimwrought, suddenly took ill and deteriorated quickly. Doctors could furnish no cure and Metzer, desperate, turned to necromancy. Using the ritual that binds a lich's phylactery, Metzer bound his daughter's soul to the prototype, simultaneously forestalling her death and furnishing the blaster with an immense power source.

description.name: Magic Weapon
description.value: The Blaster Prototype is a magic weapon that grants a +3 bonus to attack and damage rolls made with it.

description.name: Auto-Aim
description.value: If you roll less than 10 on the d20 for an attack roll with the Blaster Prototype, you can replace the roll with a 10. The prototype can choose not to grant this benefit, or to instead replace the roll with a 1 if it believes a target is unsuitable.

description.name: Blaster Mastery
description.value: You can use a Magic action to change the blaster's mastery property to that of any blaster of your choice. You can use the mastery property of the blaster, even if you don't have the Weapon Mastery feature, and it doesn't count against the number of weapons you can use. Once you change the mastery property, you can't do so again until the next dawn.

description.name: Machine Code
description.value: Using its Machine Code (DarkMatter24) language, the Blaster Prototype can cast the __Technomancy__ cantrip.

description.name: Sentience
description.value: The Blaster Prototype is a sentient Chaotic Neutral weapon with an Intelligence of 16, a Wisdom of 10, and a Charisma of 15. It has hearing and Darkvision out to 120 feet.
The prototype speaks Common (XPHB), Dwarvish (XPHB), and Machine Code (DarkMatter24), the native code-language of machines, and it can communicate with its wielder telepathically.

description.name: Personality
description.value: Though the prototype is ageless, its personality belongs to a young woman, Vantha Glimwrought, and speaks in an upbeat, chipper tone. The Prototype urges its user to travel to new places and meet interesting people; likewise, it hates being holstered, hidden away, or ignored. Even in life, Vantha was shut away and built up an insatiable wanderlust.

Vantha has complex feelings about her father, the prototype's inventor. Without question, she's grateful to be alive, but feels like her present, captive circumstances are somehow an extension of her father's overbearing nature, even after his death.
Vantha has reservations about being used on Humanoids and will never fire on a person she deems innocent.

description.name: Destroying the Blaster
description.value: The Blaster Prototype is protected by all manner of enchantments from one of history's most ingenious arcanists, rendering it impervious to damage. However, if the blaster is connected to a sufficiently large power source, like a Class 7 or 8 Dark Matter engine at the moment of a void jump, the power surge would be enough to overload the blaster and destroy it.

description.name: Heat Resistant
description.value: While wearing these boots, you have resistance to fire damage and can walk across hot liquid surfaces, such as lava, as if they were harmless ground. In addition, you can tolerate temperatures as high as 150 degrees Fahrenheit (66 degrees Celsius) without any additional protection. If you wear light or heat-resistant clothes, you can tolerate temperatures as high as 250 degrees Fahrenheit (121 degrees Celsius).

description.name: Ghostwalker
description.value: While wearing these boots, you can use an action to enter the Ethereal Plane as if under the effects of the __etherealness__ spell. You can use the boots to remain in the Ethereal Plane for up to 6 hours, all at once or in several shorter periods, each one using a minimum of 10 minutes from the duration. The boots regain 1 hour of their ability to traverse into the Ethereal Plane for every 4 hours they aren't in use or for every 50 points of fire damage dealt to you (after applying resistance).

description.name: Curse
description.value: The boots are cursed, and becoming attuned to the boots extends the curse to you; the boots' ghostly chains wrap around your spirit, preventing you from removing them. The curse can only be broken by cleansing the boots, but __remove curse__ or similar magic breaks the ghostly chains and allows you to remove the boots.

Until the curse is broken, whenever you enter the Ethereal Plane, you must succeed on a DC 11 Charisma saving throw or the boots banish you to a labyrinthine prison demiplane, while the boots remain in the space on the plane you entered the Ethereal Plane from. The DC increases by 1 for each successful saving throw and resets back to 11 on a failed saving throw. Once per hour, you can use an action to attempt to escape by making a DC 15 Intelligence check. On a success, you exit the prison demiplane and appear in an unoccupied space within 5 feet of the boots. While trapped in the prison, you are constantly stalked by five hostile __chain devils__. If you die in the prison demiplane's maze, you return to life as a baleful __chain devil__ controlled by the GM until freed from the maze (see "Cleansing the Boots of Tartarus").

description.value: If a feature grants you mastery with this armor, you gain the following benefits:

• You do not take fall damage unless you are incapacitated.
• While you are falling, you may activate (or deactivate) this cloak, with no action required. While active, your descent is slowed to 10 feet per round, and for every 10 feet you fall vertically, you can glide up to 20 feet in any horizontal direction you choose.
By grasping the two handles on this foot-wide steering wheel, you can cast the __Speedcycle__ spell. The motorcycle materializes beneath you and attaches to the steering wheel.
Once you use this item to cast the __Speedcycle__ spell, it can't be used again until the following dawn.

This set of controls, either installed in a glove, integrated onto a Datapad, or linked into a visor, allows you to control a drone. Each controller is linked to a drone, using the __Personal Drone__ stat block, and is either an Assault drone, a Medical drone, or a Shield drone.

description.name: Drone Combat
description.value: While attuned to the controller, you can use a Bonus Action to issue commands to the drone. Your drone takes its turn immediately before or after your turn each round (your choice). If you issue no commands, the drone doesn't take any actions. Once given an order, the drone continues to follow it until its task is complete.

This desiccated Spell Scroll seems to draw the moisture from your fingertips. Its cipher is ineffable, and while its meaning becomes clear as you read the runes, clarity slips away should you try to transcribe it.

As a Magic action, you can use the scroll to cast __Control Water__ without providing any Material components. The spell save DC is 15. In addition to the usual effects of the __Control Water__ spell, any water manipulated by the spell is destroyed when the spell ends. Once the spell is cast, the words on the scroll fade, and it crumbles to dust. If the casting is interrupted, the scroll is not lost.

name: Dueling Laser

description.value: A pistol intended for honorable, one-on-one duels, the Dueling Laser fires a blinding streak of light and promptly overheats. Spacers favor a Dueling Laser in their offhand for an infrequent but powerful retort.

description.name: Range
description.value: A Range weapon has a range in parentheses after the Ammunition or Thrown property. The range lists two numbers. The first is the weapon's normal range in feet, and the second is the weapon's long range. When attacking a target beyond normal range, you have Disadvantage on the attack roll. You can't attack a target beyond the long range.

description.name: Blaster
description.value: A weapon with the Blaster property is a Ranged weapon that requires no ammunition. This property counts as Ammunition.

description.name: Firearm
description.value: You don't add your ability modifier to the weapon's damage, unless otherwise stated. Firearm ammunition is destroyed upon use.

description.name: Cooldown
description.value: Because this weapon requires cooldown time between uses, you can only fire it once when you use an action, Bonus Action, or Reaction to fire it, regardless of the number of attacks you normally make. This property counts as Loading.

description.name: Light
description.value: When you take the Attack action on your turn and attack with a Light weapon, you can make one extra attack as a Bonus Action later on the same turn. That extra attack must be made with a different Light weapon, and you don't add your ability modifier to the extra attack's damage unless that modifier is negative. For example, you can attack with a Shortsword in one hand and a Dagger in the other using the Attack action and a Bonus Action, but you don't add your Strength or Dexterity modifier to the damage roll of the Bonus Action unless that modifier is negative.

description.name: Slow
description.value: If you hit a creature with this weapon and deal damage to it, you can reduce its Speed by 10 feet until the start of your next turn. If the creature is hit more than once by weapons that have this property, the Speed reduction doesn't exceed 10 feet.

description.value: This scrap of paper bears a table with space for five names. If you write a creature's name in one of the blank spaces on the table, it will shuffle the text to show their ranking as a duelist relative to all the other individuals named on the table. This appears to be calculated based on the number of duels the named individuals have won over the past year. The source of these scorecards and the rankings remains a mystery, but it appears to be linked to the Infinite Archive of Daanvi. Once all the spaces on the scorecard are filled, you cannot reveal the ranking of another name for 1 week, when all the names are magically erased.

You can't attack a target beyond the long range.

description.name: Finesse
description.value: When making an attack with a Finesse weapon, use your choice of your Strength or Dexterity modifier for the attack and damage rolls. You must use the same modifier for both rolls.

description.name: Light
description.value: When you take the Attack action on your turn and attack with a Light weapon, you can make one extra attack as a Bonus Action later on the same turn. That extra attack must be made with a different Light weapon, and you don't add your ability modifier to the extra attack's damage unless that modifier is negative. For example, you can attack with a Shortsword in one hand and a Dagger in the other using the Attack action and a Bonus Action, but you don't add your Strength or Dexterity modifier to the damage roll of the Bonus Action unless that modifier is negative.

description.name: Thrown
description.value: If a weapon has the Thrown property, you can throw the weapon to make a ranged attack, and you can draw that weapon as part of the attack. If the weapon is a Melee weapon, use the same ability modifier for the attack and damage rolls that you use for a melee attack with that weapon.

description.name: Nick
description.value: When you make the extra attack of the Light property, you can make it as part of the Attack action instead of as a Bonus Action. You can make this extra attack only once per turn.

Your base Armor Class equals 13 plus your Dexterity modifier. You can wear armor on top of your Embedded Armor, and you can use either armor to determine your AC. You can use a Shield and still gain this benefit.

You replace one of your hands with an imposing, articulated gauntlet, a Battlefist. While this weapon is installed, you are proficient with it and can't be disarmed of it. The Battlefist can hold and manipulate objects, though you can't attack with a Battlefist while holding an object with it.

Emitters in the fingertips can produce a set of razor-sharp Laser Claws. Whenever you would normally be able to draw a weapon, you can transform one or both of your hands into a set of Laser Claws, and you can revert them to their normal forms when you could normally stow a weapon. While this graft is installed, you are proficient with these weapons and can't be disarmed of them. You can't hold or otherwise manipulate a weapon, Shield, or other object with a hand that is transformed.
This convenient insulated box in your abdomen can store and chill up to six cans of Krash, potions, or similar beverages.

One of your hands is mechanical and can transform into a Repeater. Whenever you would normally be able to draw a weapon, you can transform your hand into a Repeater, and you can revert it to its normal form when you could normally stow a weapon.

While this graft is installed, you are proficient with this weapon and can't be disarmed of it. You can't hold or otherwise manipulate a weapon, Shield, or other object with a hand that is transformed.
You have a Universal Translator magic item installed within your skull and can use it at will.

This Datapad is enchanted to hold an incredible wealth of information. However, the data isn't indexed, so the Encyclopedia only provides data that it believes will be useful at any given moment. The Encyclopedia 3 charges, and regains all charges daily at dawn. When you take the Study action, you can expend 1 charge to access the Encyclopedia and gain a +20 to any Intelligence checks you make as a part of that action.

This book catalogs many hundreds of bloody ink blots. While holding the book, you can cast __Blood Print__ from it. If you consult the book as a Magic action, you can determine the following about any such print: the specific kind of creature to which the blood belongs (such as a human or a unicorn), its approximate age, sex, and its health (assessed as poor or healthy).
*Donor: Any Creature with Immunity or Resistance to Acid, Cold, Fire, Lightning, Poison, or Thunder damage*
You have Resistance to one of the following damage types to which the donor had Resistance or Immunity: Acid, Cold, Fire, Lightning, Poison, or Thunder.

An Engineer's Pack includes a Backpack, a Comm Set, a Crowbar, a Datapad, a Flashlight, a Hammer, an Igniter, a Life Suit, dozens of assorted nuts and bolts, an Omnitool, 10 rolls of Vent Tape, and a Wristwatch.
The ship gains the Engineer role.

This ship contains a bay with sufficient Escape Pods for each crew member and passenger. A creature can take the Utilize action to board an Escape Pod and eject from the ship. On a Fighter, the Pilot ejects automatically when the ship drops to 0 Mega Hit Points.

The pod travels far enough to clear any explosion of the ship and then drifts aimlessly. The pod has minimal thrusters—enough to change direction two or three times—and enough air, power, and rations to sustain a passenger for 7 days. Each Escape Pod automatically produces a distress signal that can be detected by any ship with Sensors, though such a signal only travels at the speed of light. An Escape Pod and its passenger can survive reentry on most planets.

description.name: Versatile
description.value: A Versatile weapon can be used with one or two hands. A damage value in parentheses appears with the property. The weapon deals that damage when used with two hands to make a melee attack.

description.name: Parry
description.value: When you hit a creature with this weapon and you aren't wielding a Shield, you gain a +2 bonus to your Armor Class until the start of your next turn. You can gain this bonus only once per turn.

An essential tool for galactic communication, an Etheradio transmits and receives its messages though the Ethereal Plane. This device stands over 6 feet tall (with an antenna that extends its length by an additional 3 feet) and weighs 1,000 pounds.

description.name: Transmitting
description.value: An operator can use the device as a Utilize action to transmit an audio message of up to 10 minutes to a specific Etheradio on the same plane of existence or to an etheradio station. Hundreds of stations exist, many of them earmarked for specific uses, such as streaming music or government communications. By broadcasting on an emergency station, an Etheradio can transmit a message to all other Etheradios on the same plane of existence, but it can only send such a message once per day. No matter the distance, messages take 10 minutes to reach their destination.

description.name: Receiving
description.value: The Etheradio stores the most recent 10 hours of audio it has directly received. An operator can use the device as a Utilize action to listen to stored audio or to tune into an Etheradio station.

description.name: Calibration
description.value: An Etheradio only works if it is calibrated according to its location in the universe. Calibrating this device takes 1 hour, and it must be recalibrated if it is ever moved more than 100 miles. Calibration takes into account regular cosmic motion, such as a planet's orbit.

The enormous frame, which weighs in excess of 2,000 pounds, seems less like a suit of armor and more like a mechanized, bipedal vehicle. You don't need armor training to wear this armor. You can don and doff it as a Utilize action by traveling through a series of hatches on the front of the suit. You gain the following benefits while wearing the armor.

description.name: Armor Class
description.value: While wearing this armor, your Armor Class equals 18 (your Dexterity modifier doesn't affect this number). You can use a Shield and still gain this benefit.

description.name: Size
description.value: Your size becomes Large, if it was smaller.

description.name: Mighty
description.value: You have Advantage on Strength checks and saving throws.

description.name: Integrated Battlefists
description.value: The frame has two integrated Battlefists. While wearing the armor, you have proficiency with these weapons.

description.name: Life Suit
description.value: The frame confers the benefits of a Life Suit.
This box of cards is interwoven with the threads of fate. A full deck contains a set of 52 playing cards, but other variations exist, including those with different numbers of cards and sets of dice.
Playing any game with the deck casts __Game of Fate__ (DC 17) from it. The deck can't cast this spell again until the next dawn.
While wearing this cloak, you are protected from Extreme Cold and automatically succeed the saving throw required to avoid exhaustion.

description.name: Mastery
description.value: If a feature grants you mastery with this armor, you gain all the benefits from the Drifter's Cloak description. Additionally, during your turn you can fly up to 20 feet in any direction with no action required. After doing so, you must hit a target with a melee weapon attack—or end your turn while not airborne—before you can fly again.

description.name: Stealth Disadvantage
description.value: The wearer has **Disadvantage** on Dexterity (Stealth) checks.

The ship gains the ability to dock a Fighter-size ship within it. A creature can take a Bonus Action to board the Fighter and eject it from the ship, entering the Pilot role in that ship. A Fighter can dock into a Fighter Bay as an action.

description.name: Repeatable
description.value: You can install this system more than once into a ship, depending on the ship's size: Transport (2 bays), Corvette (3 bays), Frigate (3 bays), Cruiser (4 bays), and Capital (4 bays).

name: Figurine of Wondrous Power, Byeshk Worg Pack

description.value: This set of four miniature worg statuettes is made from byeshk, a metal that is anathema to Aberrations. Each statuette is small enough to fit in a pocket. If you use a Magic action to speak the command word and throw one of the figurines to a point on the ground within 60 feet of you, the figurine becomes a living Worg for up to 1 hour. You can use one figurine or multiple simultaneously. If the space where a worg would appear is occupied by other creatures or objects, or if there isn't enough space for the worg, the figurine doesn't become a worg.
The worgs are Immune to Psychic damage, cannot be Charmed or Frightened, and their Bite attack deals an additional **2d6** damage against Aberrations.
The worgs are friendly to you and your companions. They understand your languages and obey your spoken commands. If you issue no commands, the worgs defend themselves but take no other actions.

At the end of the duration, the worgs revert to their figurine forms. A worg reverts to a figurine early if it drops to 0 Hit Points or if you use a Magic action to speak the command word again while touching it. When a worg becomes a figurine again, its property can't be used again until 7 days have passed.

Deep within your body, you have installed a miniature Arcane Warhead, whose trigger is linked to your life. When you die, this bomb detonates and destroys your body completely; as a result, you can be restored to life only by means of a __True Resurrection__ or __Wish__ spell. Each creature within a 180-foot radius Sphere centered on your body makes a DC 19 Dexterity saving throw. Creatures within a 60-foot radius that have Evasion or a similar feature can't avoid this damage. On a failed save, a creature takes 1d4 Mega (1d4 × 100) Force damage, or half as much on a successful save.
While wearing this fingerless glove, you can cast the __Finger Guns__ cantrip using your spellcasting ability. You can use the mastery property of the Finger Guns while attuned to this item.

Your mechanical hand has a retractable set of Thieves' Tools built directly into the fingers. You can extend or retract these tools as a Bonus Action. While retracted, you can conceal them perfectly. You have proficiency with Thieves' Tools while the picks are installed. If you already have proficiency, your Proficiency Bonus is doubled for any ability check you make that uses them.

description.name: Versatile
description.value: A Versatile weapon can be used with one or two hands. A damage value in parentheses appears with the property. The weapon deals that damage when used with two hands to make a melee attack.

description.name: Topple
description.value: If you hit a creature with this weapon, you can force the creature to make a Constitution saving throw (DC 8 plus the ability modifier used to make the attack roll and your Proficiency Bonus). On a failed save, the creature has the Prone condition.
This two-handed nozzle, connected to a backpack of arcane batteries, has 7 charges and regains 1d6 + 1 expended charges daily at dawn.

When you take the Attack action, you can replace one or more of your attacks with a 15-foot Cone of fire from the Flamethrower, expending 1 charge for each attack replaced in this way. Each creature in that area makes a DC 13 Dexterity saving throw, taking **3d6** Fire damage on a failed save, or half as much damage on a successful one.

description.name: Upgraded Magic Item
description.value: If you have proficiency in Martial weapons, this item grows in power as you do. The item's save DC increases when you reach level 5 (DC 15), 11 (DC 17), and 17 (DC 18).

A Flare is a foot-long, brightly colored stick with a plastic cap. You can strike the bottom of the Flare as a Utilize action, causing it to burst into a bright, colored flame, matching that of the stick. This flame burns for 10 minutes, emitting a 40-foot radius of Bright Light and Dim Light for an additional 20 feet. A Flare can burn underwater and in a vacuum.

This antique camera is loaded with a roll of film containing 1d6 + 2 blank photos. You can use a Magic action to take a picture using the camera, casting the __Flashback__ spell. The developed photo depicts the events that the spell has altered. When all of the camera's photos have been taken, it ceases to be magical.

As a Utilize action, you can throw this spherical device up to 30 feet, which detonates in a 10-foot-radius Sphere a moment after impact. Each creature within the Sphere must succeed on a DC 13 Constitution saving throw or have the Blinded and Deafened conditions until the start of your next turn. A creature that shields its eyes and ears automatically succeeds on this saving throw.

This delicate Wand hums with bound potential, and seems drawn to your fingers. While attuned to it, you cannot be *Surprised*. Additionally, whenever you roll Initiative you can choose to immediately draw this wand (no action required). If you do so, you can roll 1d4 and add the total to your Initiative score, and all creatures within 5 feet of you take 1 Lightning damage.
A Flashlight produces a 60-foot Cone of Bright Light, and Dim Light for an additional 15 feet. It can provide light for up to 4 hours, after which it must recharge for 8 hours.

description.name: Stealth Disadvantage
description.value: The wearer has **Disadvantage** on Dexterity (Stealth) checks.

As a Utilize action, you can throw this bomb up to 30 feet, where it detonates in a 10-foot-radius Sphere a moment after impact. Each creature within the Sphere must succeed on a DC 13 Constitution saving throw. On a failed save, a creature takes **3d8** Cold damage and its Speed is 0 and it has Disadvantage on attack rolls until the start of your next turn. On a successful save, a creature takes half as much damage only.

This scaled-down Datapad is packed with dozens of digital amusements and diversions that test a user's reflexes and puzzle-solving skills. If you spend a Short Rest playing on this Gamestation, you gain Advantage on the next ability check you make before you finish a Short or Long Rest.
Digital games are a variant of Gaming Sets that can be played on any Arcane Terminal, Datapad, or Gamestation. These games range from arcade-like to immersively realistic.

If you have proficiency with a tool, add your Proficiency Bonus to any ability check you make that uses the tool. If you have proficiency in a skill that's used with that check, you have Advantage on the check too.

This crystalline fragment of pure hardlight has 6 charges and regains 1d6 expended charges daily at dawn. Whenever you make a D20 Test, you can expend a number of charges up to your proficiency bonus and add that number to the number rolled on the d20, to a maximum of 20. If you use the fragment to improve an attack roll that deals damage, you can change the damage type to Force.

description.name: Magic Item Set
description.value: Attuning to multiple Gamma Fragments counts as being attuned to a single item. Add the charges into a single pool that regains 1d6 expended charges for each fragment daily at dawn.

Like many techno-magical marvels, hardlight magic was uncovered through experimentation and happenstance. However, this was not the first time hardlight had been discovered, as evidenced by the Gamma Pendant.

The pendant is a gleaming mithral medallion, set with fragments of a glowing green crystal. In ages past, the pendant was destroyed and its Gamma Fragments scattered across the 'Verse. Each of these fragments is a magic item in its own right, sought and coveted by an order of Paladins known as Gamma Knights, but the pendant itself is a thing of unparalleled power.

description.name: Incomplete Pendant
description.value: Even while missing fragments, the pendant has the following properties.

description.name: Flight
description.value: You have a Fly Speed equal to your Speed.

description.name: Starborn
description.value: You can breathe underwater or in the vacuum of space and you are unaffected by extreme temperatures and pressures (see the Glossary).

description.name: Lesser Spellcasting
description.value: The pendant has 10 charges and regains 1d6 + 4 expended charges daily at dawn. You can cast any of the Lesser Spells on the Hardlight Spells table from the pendant (save DC 18). The table indicates how many charges you must expend to cast the spell.

description.name: Completing the Pendant
description.value: If three or more Gamma Fragments are unified with the Gamma Pendant, the pendant becomes whole and gains the following additional properties.

description.name: Gamma Fragments
description.value: The pendant gains the benefits of all unified Gamma Fragments.

description.name: Greater Spellcasting
description.value: The pendant's spellcasting improves. It has 20 changes and regains 1d10 + 10 expended charges daily at dawn. You can cast any of the spells on the Hardlight Spells table from the pendant (save DC 18).

description.name: Hardlight Edge
description.value: Any weapon you wield has a +2 bonus to attack and damage rolls and can deal Force damage or the weapon's normal damage type (your choice). If the weapon already has a bonus to attack and damage rolls, use the larger bonus.

description.name: Spell Absorption
description.value: You have Advantage on saving throws you make against spells. Additionally, in response to a creature you can see within 60 feet of yourself casting a spell, you can take a Reaction to absorb that spell. The spell dissipates with no effect, the action, Bonus Action, or Reaction used to cast it is wasted, and the pendant regains a number of charges equal to the absorbed spell's level, up to a maximum of 20 charges. Once you use this property, you can't use it again until the next dawn.

description.name: Destroying the Pendant
description.value: The Gamma Pendant is impervious to damage. However, it can be shattered by smashing it between two sufficiently large hardlight constructs: each would need to be roughly the size of a small planet to achieve the desired effect.

Your arms have been replaced with the oversized limbs of a golem or a similar Construct. Your reach is 5 feet greater whenever you make an attack with a Melee weapon or Unarmed Strike. Additionally, you have Advantage on Strength checks and saving throws.

This suit of Scale Mail is made from the metallic hide of a gorgon. It is particularly valuable to anyone that wishes to visit Cazhaak Draal; while wearing this armor, you have Advantage on saving throws against any magical effect that would cause you to be Restrained or Petrified.
This patchwork, quilted cloak smells faintly of hearth and home cooking. While wearing it, you gain the following benefits.

description.name: Cozy
description.value: You automatically succeed on saving throws against extreme cold and extreme heat, and the cloak keeps you dry unless you are immersed in water.

description.name: Focus
description.value: You can use the cloak as a Spellcasting Focus for your Witch spells.

description.name: Shelter
description.value: You can cast __Rope Trick__ with a duration of 8 hours. Once used, this property can't be used again until the next dawn.

name: Grasshopper

description.value: This magic weapon deals an extra **2d10** Radiant damage on a hit and the target is pushed 10 feet away from you. Once you make an attack with this weapon, it __Overheat__. An overheated weapon can't be used to make an attack until the end of your next turn.

description.value: This device has 7 charges and regains 1d6 + 1 expended charges daily at dawn. While holding it, you can take a Magic action to expend 1 charge and cast __Levitate__ (DC 13) from it. Instead of the target rising vertically up to 20 feet, it is pulled directly toward the device, levitating in a space of your choice within 5 feet of you.

You can take a Bonus Action to violently repel a levitating target within 5 feet of yourself. In a Zero-Gravity environment, all creatures and objects are considered to be levitating. The target is pushed up to 60 away from you in a direction that you choose, ending the __Levitate__ spell. If the target contact hits an obstacle, both the target and the obstacle take **4d6** damage. The GM decides if this damage is Bludgeoning, Piercing, or Slashing.

description.name: Upgraded Magic Item
description.value: If you have proficiency in Martial weapons, this item grows in power as you do. The item's save DC increases when you reach character level 5 (DC 15), 11 (DC 17), and 17 (DC 18).

You can attach this fist-sized device to an object weighing less than 2,000 pounds as a Magic action, nullifying the object's mass as if it were targeted by the __Levitate__ spell. The nullifier functions for 10 minutes, after which it burns out and permanently ceases to function. If the object is still aloft, it gently floats to the ground.

description.name: Range
description.value: A Range weapon has a range in parentheses after the Ammunition or Thrown property. The range lists two numbers. The first is the weapon's normal range in feet, and the second is the weapon's long range. When attacking a target beyond normal range, you have Disadvantage on the attack roll. You can't attack a target beyond the long range.

description.name: Ammunition
description.value: You can use a weapon that has the Ammunition property to make a ranged attack only if you have ammunition to fire from it. The type of ammunition required is specified with the weapon's range. Each attack expends one piece of ammunition. Drawing the ammunition is part of the attack (you need a free hand to load a one-handed weapon). After a fight, you can spend 1 minute to recover half the ammunition (round down) you used in the fight; the rest is lost.

description.name: Heavy
description.value: You have Disadvantage on attack rolls with a Heavy weapon if it's a Melee weapon and your Strength score isn't at least 13 or if it's a Ranged weapon and your Dexterity score isn't at least 13.

description.name: Two-Handed
description.value: A Two-Handed weapon requires two hands when you attack with it.

description.name: Tension

After a fight, you can spend 1 minute to recover half the ammunition (round down) you used in the fight; the rest is lost.

This explosion is a 5-foot-radius Sphere centered on a point you choose within the weapon's normal range. Each creature within the Sphere makes a Dexterity saving throw (DC 8 plus your Strength or Dexterity modifier and your Proficiency Bonus). On a failed save, a creature takes the weapon's damage, but don't add your ability modifier to that damage unless that modifier is negative. On a successful save, a creature takes half as much damage. You can create an explosion only once per turn.

These rations made of troll meat slowly regenerate, promising a long-lasting food supply. A creature can use a Magic action to eat one cake. Eating a cake restores 1 Hit Point, and the cake provides enough nourishment to sustain a creature for one day.

A pack contains a maximum of 10 cakes. So long as at least 1 cake remains uneaten and unspoiled, the pack regenerates 1d6 cakes per day. If you take Fire or Acid damage while carrying a pack of Grist Cakes, 1d4 cakes permanently spoil and will no longer regenerate.
The ship gains the Gunner role.

When you fail an attempt to hack a device, you can use this graft to reroll it, potentially turning failure into success. You must use the new roll, and you can't use this graft to reroll again until you finish a Long Rest.

This magic bracer has 20 charges. You can expend 1 charge as a Magic action to produce a Hardlight Dart to your open hand. If unused, this dart evaporates into light after 24 hours. The bracer regains 1d10 + 5 charges daily at dawn.

name: Hardlight Dart

You also count as one size larger when determining your carrying capacity.

description.value: This sunstaff was once carried by a heretical avia-ra apologist. When the staff deals the Bludgeoning damage of its __Bludgeon__ mastery property, it deals an extra **1d6** Radiant damage.

description.value: Attuning to this sunstaff and an Ankh of Ra and Solar Wings of Ra counts as being attuned to a single item. If you are attuned to the sunstaff and one of these items, you can use a Magic action to unleash a blinding beam of light in a 5-foot-wide, 60-foot-long Line. Each creature in the Line must make a DC 15 Constitution saving throw or be Blinded until the end of your next turn. The staff can't be used in this way again until the next dawn.

You can pause recording, delete a recorded scene, or play back a recorded scene as a Magic action.

You can use your Dexterity modifier instead of your Strength modifier for the attack and damage rolls of your Unarmed Strikes. This 3-foot-long metal board produces a low hum and curiously hovers over any surface. You can ride the board or dismount it as a Bonus Action. While riding the board, your Speed increases by 10 feet, you ignore Difficult Terrain, and can move above the surface of liquids without sinking. The board can't scale an incline greater than 45 degrees unless it is in a zero-gravity environment.
You can use your choice of a Dexterity (*Acrobatics*) check or a Charisma (*Performance*) check to perform tricks on the board.

As a Utilize action, you can set a Hunting Trap, which is a sawtooth steel ring that snaps shut when a creature steps on a pressure plate in the center. The trap is affixed by a heavy chain to an immobile object, such as a tree or a spike driven into the ground. A creature that steps on the plate must succeed on a Dexterity saving throw or take **1d4** Piercing damage and have its Speed reduced to 0 until the start of its next turn. Thereafter, until the creature breaks free of the trap, its movement is limited by the length of the chain (typically 3 feet). A creature can use its action to make a Strength (*Athletics*) check against your Traps save DC, freeing itself or another creature within its reach on a success. Each failed check deals 1 Piercing damage to the trapped creature. It takes a Utilize action to recover the Hunting Trap.

This limited-edition can of Krash-branded energy drink was discontinued decades ago for being too extreme (as well as for hazardous side effects from its magical additives). When you drink this potion, a jittery feeling rushes to your extremities. You can take an additional action this turn, which can be used to take only the Attack (one attack only), Dash, Disengage, Hide, or Utilize action. You also have Advantage on all attack rolls and ability checks you make until the end of this turn. The feeling of energy is then replaced by lethargy, and you can't gain the benefits of this potion again for 1 hour.

Potions are often loaded into syringes instead of consumed from a bottle. You can load a potion into a Hypodermic Needle as a Bonus Action and administer it to another creature as a Bonus Action. If the creature is unwilling, it must succeed a Dexterity saving throw (DC 8 plus your Intelligence modifier and Proficiency Bonus) to avoid the needle.
An Igniter produces a small flame, which you can use to light a Candle, Torch, or campfire.

You have installed thrusters into your legs and back. Once on each of your turns, when you move at least 15 feet in a straight Line, you can move up to 10 additional feet in that direction without spending movement. Alternatively, you can spend 10 feet of movement to jump 10 feet vertically.
*Donor: Medium or Larger Aberration*
You have spliced aberrant genetics into your body, which have altered your internal organs. Any Critical Hit against you becomes a normal hit.
You have replaced your eyes with sensors that can see in the dark. You gain Darkvision with a range of 60 feet.

This colorful, jellyfish-like blob has been carefully cultivated by Quickstone's schoolmaster, Tragomir "Ink" Narathun, to impart a full curriculum to its host—though he has yet to convince anyone to partake. To attune to this item, you must hold it to one ear for the full Attunement period, during which time its stringy tentacles reach inside your ear canal and secure the aide in place. The symbiont does not impair your hearing while it is attached.

description.name: Spells
description.value: The symbiont has 4 charges. You can use a Magic action to expend 1 or more of its charges to cast one of the following spells (save DC 15) from it: __Enhance Ability__ (2 charges) or __Comprehend Languages__ (1 charge).
The symbiont regains 1d4 expended charges daily at dawn.

description.name: Symbiotic Nature
description.value: The aide can't be removed from you while you're attuned to it, and you can't voluntarily end your Attunement to it. If you're targeted by a spell that ends a curse, your Attunement to the aide ends, and it detaches from your ear.

An Interface Rig is often necessary to gain unauthorized access to a system.

The condition ends early immediately for a creature after it makes an attack roll, deals damage, or casts a spell.

Kharash's Promise is a 3-foot long warhorn forged of demonglass and black iron. A trickle of boiling blood constantly drips from its widest end. While holding this Horn, you gain a +3 bonus to spell attack rolls and to the saving throw DCs of your Bard spells.

description.name: Thaumaturgic Clarion
description.value: If you blow Kharash's Promise, the sound it produces can be heard by all creatures within 1 mile.

Once this property is used, you cannot do so again until 13 days have passed.

On a hit, the second creature takes the weapon's damage, but don't add your ability modifier to that damage unless that modifier is negative. You can make this extra attack only once per turn.

An elegant weapon for a more enlightened age, the Laser Sword which projects a fixed-length laser from a metal hilt when activated. Its weightless blade makes for an agile weapon, capable of slicing through many materials. It could even stop a blaster bolt, but alas, one would need superhuman reflexes to intercept incoming plasma.

description.name: Finesse
description.value: When making an attack with a Finesse weapon, use your choice of your Strength or Dexterity modifier for the attack and damage rolls. You must use the same modifier for both rolls.

description.name: Versatile
description.value: A Versatile weapon can be used with one or two hands. A damage value in parentheses appears with the property. The weapon deals that damage when used with two hands to make a melee attack.

description.name: Sap
description.value: If you hit a creature with this weapon, that creature has Disadvantage on its next attack roll before the start of your next turn.

You've installed a defibrillator, or a similar piece of technology, into your vital organs. If you are dead or have 0 Hit Points at the start of your turn, the unit jolts you back to life with a surge of electricity. You revive with 1 Hit Point. This graft can't revive you if you lack a heart, have died of old age, or are missing vital organs.
Once this graft activates, it can't do so again until you finish a Long Rest.
*Donor: Any Creature with the Standing Leap Trait or Pounce Action*
The distance of your Long and High Jumps increases by 10 feet (this extra distance costs movement as normal). You suffer no penalty for making a standing High or Long Jump.
You can take a Reaction when you fall to reduce any damage you take from the fall by an amount equal to five times your Proficiency Bonus.

Hags, oni, doppelgangers, and more all spin webs of intrigue in Droaam, and the richest warlords have found ways to ensure their safety against infiltrators. This 4-inch-diameter, dull-gray glass lens is said to have been ground with a stone fallen from the moon Lharvion. When you speak its command word, the lens' power activates for 1 minute. If you look at a creature through the lens while it is active, you see ghostly images of every shape that creature has taken within the last 24 hours. The lens reveals shapes taken using innate magical abilities, as well as Illusion and Transmutation spells such as Disguise Self and Polymorph. It does not reveal mundane disguises. Once this property is used, it cannot be used again until 7 days have passed.

This one-piece jumpsuit comes equipped with a domed glass helmet. While wearing it, you can breathe underwater or in the vacuum of space for up to 24 hours at a time. The suit also protects you from extreme temperatures and pressures (see the Glossary), inhaled poisons and gasses, and contagions. You can wear the suit underneath a suit of armor. To replenish its air supply, the suit must be removed for 2 hours.

Providing a ship with air, heat, and artificial gravity, Life Support is a ship's most essential system. If Life Support is disabled, a temporary backup will be engaged, providing the ship with air and heat for up to 1 hour, but not restoring artificial gravity.
For less conventional starships, such as those shaped as galleons, the Life Support extends a bubble of heat and atmosphere around the entire ship.

An Engineer (or a creature that hacks into the ship computer) can take the Use System action to disable Life Support. Depending on the ship, this may allow them to vent the atmosphere from parts of the ship, disable the artificial gravity (rendering the entire ship a Zero-Gravity environment, if it's in space), or disable the ship's heating and cooling.

This 10-foot-wide, 10-foot-long, 6-inch-thick platform of wood and steel levitates 5 feet off the ground and remains horizontal so long as it is within 20 feet of an operational track of lightning rail conductor stones. The platform can carry up to 2000 pounds. If it becomes overloaded, it drops to the ground, unable to levitate.

The platform is equipped with a 'pump' in its center that can be used to move it along the track of conductor stones. As a Magic action, a creature touching the pump can expend a spell slot of 1st-level or higher to cause the platform to continuously move either forwards or backwards along the conductor stone track at a speed of 30 feet. A creature with the Mark of Passage does not need to expend a spell slot to cause the platform to move.

Once moving, the platform will move in the chosen direction for one hour, or until a creature touching the pump uses a Magic action to cause the platform to stop. If stopped in this way, a creature must expend another spell slot as a Magic action to start the platform moving again.

If the platform encounters an obstacle while moving, it will continue to push against the obstacle unless stopped with a Magic action. Obstacles that weigh less than the total weight of the platform and its cargo will be pushed in front of the platform.

This Plate Armor appears to be made of stone slabs carved with alien symbols. It is strangely warm to the touch. To attune to this item, you must wear it for the entire Attunement period, during which the stone plates fuse with your skin.

While wearing this armor, you have a +1 bonus to Armor Class, and you have Resistance to nonmagical Bludgeoning, Piercing, and Slashing damage. Additionally, the armor hardens under extreme impact; if you take 20 or more nonmagical Bludgeoning, Piercing, or Slashing damage from one damage roll (after accounting for your Resistance), you are Petrified until the end of your next turn.

description.name: # Symbiotic Nature
description.value: The armor can't be removed from you while you're attuned to it, and you can't voluntarily end your Attunement to it. If you're targeted by a spell that ends a curse, your Attunement to the armor ends, and it detaches from you.
The armor requires fresh blood be fed to it. Immediately after you finish any Long Rest, you must either feed half of your remaining Hit Dice to the armor (round up) or take 1 level of Exhaustion.
This foot-long device records and replays audio, organizing entries by date. It can store up to 72 hours of audio before it automatically begins purging the earliest entries.

Your brain has been augmented with an algorithmic processing unit. You can add half your Proficiency Bonus (round down), to any Intelligence ability check you make that uses a skill proficiency you lack and doesn't already include your Proficiency Bonus. Additionally, you know Machine Code (DarkMatter24), the native code-language of machines. Due to this language, you know the __Technomancy__ cantrip. Intelligence, Wisdom, or Charisma is your spellcasting ability for the spells you cast with this trait (choose the ability when you select the feat).

With the right expertise and rituals, a songbird harpy's magic can be suffused throughout her plumage. While wearing this magical feather, you find that people can be much more agreeable—all they need is a little push. When you make a Charisma (*Persuasion*) check, you can choose to have Advantage on the check (no action required). Once this property is used, the feather loses its luster and becomes nonmagical.

name: Magnus

description.value: This impressive handgun weighs almost twice that of a Repeater. Its infamous heft, recoil, and stopping power make it a favorite of spacers that accept no compromises.

description.name: Range
description.value: A Range weapon has a range in parentheses after the Ammunition or Thrown property. The range lists two numbers. The first is the weapon's normal range in feet, and the second is the weapon's long range. When attacking a target beyond normal range, you have Disadvantage on the attack roll. You can't attack a target beyond the long range.

description.value: A weapon with the Blaster property is a Ranged weapon that requires no ammunition. This property counts as Ammunition.

description.name: Firearm
description.value: You don't add your ability modifier to the weapon's damage, unless otherwise stated. Firearm ammunition is destroyed upon use.

description.name: Cooldown
description.value: Because this weapon requires cooldown time between uses, you can only fire it once when you use an action, Bonus Action, or Reaction to fire it, regardless of the number of attacks you normally make. This property counts as Loading.

description.name: Heavy
description.value: You have Disadvantage on attack rolls with a Heavy weapon if it's a Melee weapon and your Strength score isn't at least 13 or if it's a Ranged weapon and your Dexterity score isn't at least 13.

description.name: Overheat
description.value: If you hit a target with this weapon, you can overcharge the weapon. If you do so, the target takes extra damage of the weapon's type equal to your Proficiency Bonus. The weapon then Overheats. An Overheated weapon can't be used again to make an attack until the end of your next turn.

description.value: A ship's Manipulators are collapsible devices that allow the ship to interact with ships and objects, sometimes resembling arms, tentacles, or extensions of the hull. An Engineer can take the Use System action to use the Manipulators on a target within 500 feet of the ship. It can transport an object into the ship's cargo hold, clear space debris, open a hatch on a ship, or push a Mega-sized target smaller than the ship up to 1,000 feet away from the ship.

A Marine's Pack includes a Backpack, a Bedroll, Binoculars, a Comm Set, a Concussion Grenade, a Crowbar, a Flashlight, an Igniter, a Life Suit, 10 days of Rations, Rope, a Tactical Vest, and a roll of Vent Tape.

Though most worgs prefer to fight with their teeth or steel jaws, there are those that desire to wield a Dhakaani blade against their enemies. This ornate mask is set with magical gems that focus your subconscious thoughts into a subtle form of telekinesis, allowing you greater control over objects you hold in your teeth.

While wearing the mask, you can use your mouth to wield any Melee weapon that does not have the Heavy, Two-Handed, or Reach properties. If you use the mask to wield a weapon that has Versatile, you can only wield it as if you were using a single hand.

description.name: Reach
description.value: A Reach weapon adds 5 feet to your reach when you attack with it, as well as when determining your reach for Opportunity Attacks with it.

description.name: Two-Handed
description.value: A Two-Handed weapon requires two hands when you attack with it.

description.name: Topple
description.value: If you hit a creature with this weapon, you can force the creature to make a Constitution saving throw (DC 8 plus the ability modifier used to make the attack roll and your Proficiency Bonus). On a failed save, the creature has the Prone condition.

The minotaurs of Droaam have no issues navigating the winding streets of the region's great cities, and their understanding has been captured in these fragile maps. When you speak the map's command word while in the city for which it was made, you can add twice your Proficiency Bonus to any Wisdom (*Survival*) checks made to navigate or track a creature through the city for 1 hour. At the end of the hour, the map crumbles to dust.

This small embroidered pouch is said to contain the cast-off goods discarded by the Merchant of Misthaven, an archfey of Thelanis. When you reach into the pouch, you can pull out a random trinket (see page 46 of the 2024 version of the fifth edition Player's Handbook or any other random trinket table of your choice). A trinket pulled from this pouch disappears when you pull another trinket from the pouch.

description.name: Stealth Disadvantage
description.value: The wearer has **Disadvantage** on Dexterity (Stealth) checks.

This scanner bears an illuminated screen on one side. While holding it, you can determine the location of any creatures or objects within 60 feet of you that have moved since the end of your last turn, even if they have the Invisible condition or have Total Cover from you. A creature that has the Hide action's Invisible condition, however, avoids detection by the tracker.

description.name: Graze
description.value: If your attack roll with this weapon misses a creature, you can deal damage to that creature equal to the ability modifier you used to make the attack roll. This damage is the same type dealt by the weapon, and the damage can be increased only by increasing the ability modifier.

This capsule contains a swarm of short-lived nanobots designed to destroy, repair, or amass together into a creature. The nanobots come in three varieties: Deconstructive, Reconstructive, and Transformative. All three sets of nanobots are indistinguishable; you can determine the capsule's contents with a DC 15 Intelligence (*Technology*) check.

You can take the Magic action to open and throw the canister. Target one creature, object, or unoccupied space within 30 feet of yourself. If the canister is thrown at an unoccupied space, the nanobots cover a 5-foot-square area. The effect is determined by the type of nanobots.

description.name: Deconstructive Nanobots
description.value: The target must succeed on a DC 15 Dexterity saving throw or be covered with nanobots. At the start of each of its turns, a target covered with the nanobots takes **1d10** Necrotic damage which ignores Resistance and Immunity. After 1 minute, the nanobots deactivate permanently.

The nanobots come in three varieties: Deconstructive, Reconstructive, and Transformative. All three sets of nanobots are indistinguishable; you can determine the capsule's contents with a DC 15 Intelligence (*Technology*) check.

You can take the Magic action to open and throw the canister. Target one creature, object, or unoccupied space within 30 feet of yourself. If the canister is thrown at an unoccupied space, the nanobots cover a 5-foot-square area. The effect is determined by the type of nanobots.

description.name: Reconstructive Nanobots
description.value: The target is covered in nanobots. At the start of each of its turns, the target regains 1d6 Hit Points. After 1 minute, the nanobots deactivate permanently.

All three sets of nanobots are indistinguishable; you can determine the capsule's contents with a DC 15 Intelligence (*Technology*) check.

description.name: Transformative Nanobots
description.value: The nanobots assemble into a Nanite Swarm at the point of impact. The swarm is friendly to you and your companions, understands your languages, and obeys your spoken commands. If you issue no commands, the swarm takes the Dodge action and moves to avoid danger. After 8 hours, or after the nanite swarm drops to 0 Hit Points, the nanites deactivate.

description.name: Finesse
description.value: When making an attack with a Finesse weapon, use your choice of your Strength or Dexterity modifier for the attack and damage rolls. You must use the same modifier for both rolls.

description.name: Slow
description.value: If you hit a creature with this weapon and deal damage to it, you can reduce its Speed by 10 feet until the start of your next turn. If the creature is hit more than once by weapons that have this property, the Speed reduction doesn't exceed 10 feet.

Enterprising artificers are keen to bridge the gap between the tallest and the smallest Droaamites. Ogre Tines are just one example of the myriad devices designed to help giantkin interact with kobolds and goblins. Each set consists of five foot-long iron nails bound by a ring at their tops. When held in one hand, the nails can bend and twist as if they were tiny fingers. While using the tines, creatures of Medium size or larger that would normally have Disadvantage on Dexterity (*Sleight of Hand*) checks instead do not have Disadvantage.

This multipurpose gadget contains a plethora of useful tools: small knives of various sizes, a small hammer, screwdrivers, a file, a bottle opener, a small saw, a wrench, a can opener, a wire-cutter, and a small set of pliers.

This thin rope belt is woven with strands of white and black oni hair. While wearing the belt, you can speak its command word to cause your height to become exactly 5 ft. 10 inches, and your size to become Medium. You can speak the command word again to return to your natural size.

The original Oni Braid was designed by a hobgoblin artificer who wished to see eye to eye with all the people of Droaam, though it's rumored that she designed it to set everyone's height to be one inch less than her own.

Despite being separated from its original owner, the lost arm of the daelkyr Orlassk can grant its wielder a sliver of the Lord of Stone's magic; enough power to reshape the world. To attune to this symbiont, you must hold it against one of your arms for the full Attunement period, during which time its stone skin softens and envelops your limb.

description.name: Random Properties
description.value: This Artifact has the following random properties, which you can determine by rolling on the tables in the "Artifacts" section of the Dungeon Master's Guide:

• 2 [minor beneficial](https://5e.tools/tables.html#artifact%20properties%3B%20minor%20beneficial%20properties_xdmg) properties
• 2 [minor detrimental](https://5e.tools/tables.html#artifact%20properties%3B%20minor%20detrimental%20properties_xdmg) properties
• 1 [major beneficial](https://5e.tools/tables.html#artifact%20properties%3B%20major%20beneficial%20properties_xdmg) property
• 1 [major detrimental](https://5e.tools/tables.html#artifact%20properties%3B%20major%20detrimental%20properties_xdmg) property

description.name: # Voice of the Daelkyr
description.value: You can speak with any Aberration as if you shared a language.

description.name: # Command Aberration
description.value: As a Magic action, you can cast __Dominate Monster__ on an Aberration (save DC 18). Once this property is used, you cannot do so again until the next dawn.

description.name: # Petrifying Touch
description.value: The power of the stone shaper flows from you—despite what you may will. Any creature that you touch with your stone fingertips is affected as if you had cast __Flesh to Stone__ (spell save DC 18). You do not need to concentrate on the effect, and you cannot choose to end it.

description.name: # Stone Speaking
description.value: As a Magic action, you imbue stones in an immobile 30-foot Emanation with limited sentience, giving them the ability to communicate with you. You can question stones about events in the effects area within the past day, gaining information about creatures that have passed, items that might have been removed from the area, and other circumstances. If an earth elemental or Petrified creature is in the area, you can communicate with it as if you shared a common language, but you gain no magical ability to influence it.

description.name: # Greater Symbiotic Nature
description.value: The arm can't be removed from you while you're attuned to it, and you can't voluntarily end your Attunement to it. Your Attunement to the arm can only be ended by a __Wish__ spell.

You have installed an internal generator to temporarily accelerate your reaction speed. You can use a Bonus Action to fire up your Overdrive Module. For the next minute, time appears to move in slow motion. When you activate this graft and as a Bonus Action on subsequent turns, you gain Advantage on the next attack roll or ability check you make before the end of your turn. Additionally, you can use your Reaction to gain Advantage on a Dexterity saving throw or to impose Disadvantage on an attack made against you by a creature you can see.
Once you activate this graft, you can't do so again until you finish a Long Rest.
*Donor: Giant*

You have replaced your arms with a Giant's massive limbs. Your reach is 5 feet greater whenever you make an attack with a Melee weapon or Unarmed Strike. Additionally, you have Advantage on Strength checks and saving throws.

description.name: Finesse
description.value: When making an attack with a Finesse weapon, use your choice of your Strength or Dexterity modifier for the attack and damage rolls. You must use the same modifier for both rolls.

description.name: Light
description.value: When you take the Attack action on your turn and attack with a Light weapon, you can make one extra attack as a Bonus Action later on the same turn. That extra attack must be made with a different Light weapon, and you don't add your ability modifier to the extra attack's damage unless that modifier is negative. For example, you can attack with a Shortsword in one hand and a Dagger in the other using the Attack action and a Bonus Action, but you don't add your Strength or Dexterity modifier to the damage roll of the Bonus Action unless that modifier is negative.

description.name: Parry
description.value: When you hit a creature with this weapon and you aren't wielding a Shield, you gain a +2 bonus to your Armor Class until the start of your next turn. You can gain this bonus only once per turn.

A Personality Module contains a neural trace of someone's entire personality: their core memories, manner of speaking, likes and dislikes, and even skills. While this module is installed, you are proficient in two skills, know two languages, and have a personality trait inherent to the personality. Each Personality Module offers a different set of skills, languages, and personality traits, according to whom it was modeled after.

You attach a muscular, prehensile tail, which you can use to make Unarmed Strikes. You can use your Dexterity modifier instead of your Strength modifier for the attack and damage rolls of your Unarmed Strikes. When you deal damage with an Unarmed Strike, you can deal Bludgeoning damage equal to 1d6 plus your Strength or Dexterity modifier instead of the strike's normal damage. Additionally, you can hold and manipulate objects and weapons with your tail, but you can't make attacks with weapons held by your tail or wield a Shield with your tail and gain its benefits.

The Engineer can take the Use System action to launch, dock, or control the Probe. The Probe has 5 Mega Hit Points, AC 12, a Speed of 1,500 feet, and 360-degree Maneuverability. The Engineer can see and hear through the Probe's sensors and also detect a wide variety of other metrics, such as levels of temperature, gravity, and radiation.

Made of an exotic crystal, a Psionic Piercing resonates with the underlying psionic fields in the 'Verse and enables its wearer to pull against it. These piercings might be rings, studs, bars, or any other form, and can be worn anywhere on the body.

Attuning to multiple Psionic Piercings counts as attuning to a single magic item, up to a maximum of 7 piercings. For each piercing you are attuned to, you gain one psionic energy point, which you can spend to gain the following properties. You can change which properties you have selected daily at dawn.
If a Psionic Piercing property gives you the ability to cast a spell, Intelligence, Wisdom, or Charisma is your spellcasting ability for these spells (chosen when you choose the property).

description.name: Empathy (Costs 1 Point)
description.value: You can take the Magic action to probe the mind of a creature you can see within 30 feet of you. You learn the creature's emotional state.

description.name: Fly (Costs 5 Points)
description.value: You have a Fly Speed equal to your Speed.

description.name: Influence (Costs 2 Points)
description.value: You can cast the __Detect Thoughts__ and __Suggestion__ spells once each. Once you cast one of these spells with this property, you can't cast that spell with it again until the next dawn.

description.name: Minor Kinesis (Costs 1 Point)
description.value: You learn the __Mage Hand__ cantrip, and the hand is invisible when you cast the cantrip with this trait. Intelligence, Wisdom, or Charisma is your spellcasting ability for this spell when you cast them with this property (choose when you attune to this item).

description.name: Prescience (Costs 2 Points)
description.value: You can glimpse the future as a Bonus Action. The GM reveals something that will likely occur within the next minute. You have Advantage on D20 Tests that pertain to the event you glimpsed. You can use this property a number of times equal to the number of Psionic Piercings to which you are attuned and regain all expended uses daily at dawn.

description.name: Psiblast (Costs 5 Points)
description.value: You emit a burst of psionic energy in a 60-foot Cone. Each creature in that area must make an Intelligence saving throw. The DC equals 8 + your Proficiency Bonus + your Intelligence, Wisdom, or Charisma modifier (your choice). On a failed save, a creature takes **6d8** Psychic damage and has the Stunned condition for 1 minute. On a successful save, it takes half as much damage only. A creature Stunned by this effect makes another Intelligence saving throw at the end of each of its turns, ending the effect on itself on a success. Once you use this property, you can't use it again until the next dawn.

description.name: Psychic Resistance (Costs 1 Point)
description.value: You have resistance to Psychic damage.

description.name: Telepathy (Costs 1 Point)
description.value: You can speak telepathically to any creature you can see within 60 feet of yourself. Your telepathic utterances are in a language you know, and the creature understands you only if it knows that language. Your communication doesn't give the creature the ability to respond to you telepathically.

description.name: Telekinesis (Costs 3 Points)
description.value: You can cast __Telekinesis__ once without expending a spell slot. You regain the ability to cast it in this way daily at dawn.

description.name: Third Eye (Costs 3 Points)
description.value: You have Blindsight with a range of 20 feet.

description.name: Shift
description.value: If you hit a creature with this weapon, you can immediately move 10 feet without provoking Opportunity Attacks.

When directed at an object within 5 feet as a Utilize action, the device measures and displays many of that object's intrinsic properties, including its temperature, density, boiling point, freezing point, conductivity, and viscosity.

All creatures within 5 feet of you (including you) must make a Constitution saving throw against your spell save DC. On a failed save, affected creatures take **1d4** Thunder damage for each level of the spell you cast, and are Deafened until the end of their next turn.

Though it resembles stone jewelry, the torc is in fact a simple symbiont which grants a limited form of control over earth and the ability to manipulate quickstone without the usual rituals. To attune to it, you must wear it around your neck for the full Attunement period, during which time it coils around your throat like a snake.

description.value: As an Action, you can use the symbiote to cast __Mold Earth__ XGE or Meld into Stone. Once you use the torc to cast __Meld into Stone__, the spell can't be cast in this way until the next dusk.

description.name: # Symbiotic Nature
description.value: The torc can't be removed from you while you're attuned to it, and you can't voluntarily end your Attunement to it. If you're targeted by a spell that ends a curse, your Attunement to the torc ends, and it uncoils from around your neck.

Replacement limbs can look like the original limb, or can appear metallic or mechanical. A Replacement organ or limb takes up one body slot relevant to it; for example, a troll's hand takes the Arms slot and a replacement kidney takes up the Internal slot. While wearing this ring, you can use a Magic action to expend 1 of its 3 charges to cast the spell __Paradox__ from it. The ring becomes nonmagical when you use the last charge.

While attuned to this ring, you can breathe underwater or in the vacuum of space. The ring also protects you from extreme temperatures and pressures (see the Glossary). Additionally, in zero-gravity environments, you gain a Fly Speed equal to your Speed.

description.name: Illusory Script
description.value: You can expend 1 charge as an action to cast the __illusory script__ spell from the ring.

description.name: Moon Shades
description.value: You can expend 2 charges as an action to cast the __mirror image__ spell from the ring.

description.value: You can expend 1 to 3 charges as an action. For each charge you expend, you manifest a glittering burst of silvery light at a point you can see within 60 feet of you. Each creature within a 5-foot cube originating from that point must succeed on a DC 15 Dexterity saving throw, taking **2d4** force damage on a failed save, or half as much damage on a successful one. On a failed save, a creature also glows silver until the end of your next turn, and the next attack made against the creature while it is glowing has advantage.
